title: Multi-Cloud Identity and Access Anomalies

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudtrail` events with `OR index=azure OR index=gcp` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.4.12 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudtrail` traffic without `OR index=azure OR index=gcp`. Confirm UC-4.4.12 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudtrail` collected via Combined cloud TAs, identity lookup tables; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
app: Combined cloud TAs, identity lookup tables
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" OR index=azure OR index=gcp
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.12_multi_cloud_identity_and_12"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.4.12 — Multi-Cloud Identity and Access Anomalies: queries multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) `aws:cloudtrail` for search criteria `OR index=azure OR index=gcp` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), detecting 'Multi-Cloud Identity and Access Anomalies' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.4.12 drives high-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Normalize principal IDs to a common identity (e.g. email). Ingest IAM and sign-in events from all clouds. Baseline activity per identity; alert on first-time cross-cloud activity or impossible travel across cloud regions. Use for insider threat and compromise detection.
visualization: Table (identity, clouds, activity count), Sankey (identity to cloud to action), Timeline (cross-cloud events).
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure Combined cloud TAs, identity lookup tables with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Normalize principal IDs to a common identity (e.g. email). Ingest IAM and sign-in events from all clouds. Baseline activity per identity; alert on first-time cross-cloud activity or impossible travel across cloud regions. Use for insider threat and compromise detection.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" OR index=azure OR index=gcp
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.12_multi_cloud_identity_and_12"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=aws` to detect multi-cloud identity and access anomalies. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_12_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (identity, clouds, activity count), Sankey (identity to cloud to action), Timeline (cross-cloud events)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Combined cloud TAs, identity lookup tables and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of multi-cloud identity and access anomalies so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
